record.paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
record.context_brief: Finite length of rotational bands from coherence angle
record.original_question: What quantitative coherence-angle and spontaneous-symmetry-breaking criteria determine how many states a regular nuclear rotational band can sustain before the band is cut off by band crossing, quasiparticle alignment, magnetic rotation, or band termination?

evidence.quote: In analogy, there exists a coherence angle∆ψ that limits the resolution of the wave functions of collective rotation, which are called ”coherent” because the nucleons are correlated such that a common orderly motion results.
The correlation angle sets the limit how much phase ψJ/ℏ the rotational wave can function acquire and such it restricts the number of states in the rotational band to ∆I∼ 2/∆ψ.
The regular level sequence of the state band stops aroundI = 12, where it is crossed by another band containing a pair of i13/2 neutrons that aligned their spins with the rotational axis.
Band termination is a second phenomenon how the finite length of bands materializes in transitional nuclei.
In case of rotation, the coherence angle limits the number of states in a rotational band, which is cut-oﬀ by band crossing or band termination.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an atomic nucleus exhibiting collective rotational motion, modeled as a quantum rotor whose low-lying excited states form a rotational band of angular-momentum eigenstates with quantum numbers I = I_0, I_0+2, I_0+4, .... Treat the rotational wave function as a coherent superposition of orientation states, and define a coherence angle Δψ as the angular resolution to which the orientation of the rotating mean-field shape can be quantum-mechanically defined; the rotational wave function can therefore acquire only a phase ψI/ℏ bounded by this coherence, restricting the number of band members to ΔI ∼ 2/Δψ.

A regular (state) band of finite length is observed to terminate by one of the following mechanisms:
(i) band crossing by an aligned two-quasiparticle configuration (e.g., a pair of high-j neutrons or protons whose intrinsic spins align with the rotation axis);
(ii) quasiparticle alignment within the band itself;
(iii) a transition to magnetic rotation (shears mechanism); or
(iv) band termination, in which the available valence-space angular momentum is exhausted in a non-collective stretched configuration.

Problem. Derive, from microscopic considerations of spontaneous symmetry breaking of rotational symmetry by the nuclear mean field together with the coherence-angle estimate ΔI ∼ 2/Δψ, quantitative criteria expressing the maximum spin I_max (equivalently, the maximum number of band members) that a regular rotational band can sustain before being cut off by each of the mechanisms (i)–(iv). The criteria should relate I_max to intrinsic nuclear parameters (such as the deformation parameter β, the moment of inertia ℐ, single-particle level density at the Fermi surface, pairing gap Δ, and Fermi-surface high-j orbital occupations) and predict, for a given nucleus and configuration, which of the four cutoff mechanisms occurs first.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a derivation that unifies the coherence-angle estimate ΔI ∼ 2/Δψ with quantitative spontaneous-symmetry-breaking criteria predicting the cutoff of rotational bands by band crossing, quasiparticle alignment, magnetic rotation, or band termination. Standard references describe each mechanism phenomenologically (e.g. terminating bands losing collectivity at maximum spin), but a unified quantitative criterion appears not to have been established. The status is best regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Theory of nuclear rotational bands
status_evidence.snippet: Microscopic theoretical frameworks describe rotational bands but do not give a unified coherence-angle criterion for band cutoff.
status_evidence.claim: No unified quantitative coherence-angle criterion is reported in standard treatments of rotational bands.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear Collective Motion (SpringerLink)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses collective rotational motion and band termination phenomenologically; configurations gradually lose collectivity and terminate at maximum supported spin.
status_evidence.claim: Band-termination mechanisms are described phenomenologically, not via a unified coherence-angle derivation.
